title: Platform systems & services — team wiki, playbooks, dashboards, runbooks and roadmap
author: Aisha Rahman
content:
Overview:

This document is the canonical team wiki entry for the Platform (systems & services) area. It consolidates: the systems inventory, common how-tos, dashboards & alerting conventions, primary runbooks, recent retrospectives and the near-term roadmap. It is intended as a polished, consumable reference for oncall engineers, platform owners, and partner teams.

Key goals:
- Keep production SLOs met with predictable operational playbooks.
- Reduce time-to-recovery for common incidents with clear runbooks.
- Maintain a single source of truth for dashboard coverage and alerting rules.
- Surface roadmap priorities that materially improve platform reliability and cost.

1) Systems & services inventory (high level)

Core platform services (owner, primary SLO):
- control-plane-api (team: platform-core) — SLO: availability 99.95% monthly; p95 API latency < 200ms
- scheduler-service (team: platform-core) — SLO: job dispatch success 99.9%
- kv-cache (service: redis-cluster) (team: infra-caching) — SLO: 99.9% availability; p99 latency < 10ms
- inference-router (team: serving-routing) — SLO: request success 99.9%; p95 latency < 250ms
- telemetry-ingest (team: observability) — SLO: event ingestion 99.5%
- tenant-portal (team: platform-ui) — SLO: availability 99.9%

Service ownership and contact patterns:
- Each service above has a documented owner on the team roster page and a dedicated Slack channel named #svc-<service> (e.g., #svc-control-plane-api). For incident escalation, follow the oncall rota in section 7.

2) How-tos & quick reference

Deployments:
- CI deploys are controlled by the platform-cd pipeline in GitLab (project: infra/platform-cd). To run a canary deploy:
  1. Create canary tag (git tag -a canary-<YYYYMMDD> -m "canary")
  2. Trigger pipeline variable CANARY=true in GitLab UI or cli: glab pipeline run -p CANARY=true
  3. Monitor canary via dashboard: dash -> "Canaries / control-plane-api"
  4. Rollback: glab pipeline cancel <id> and revert tag.

Service debugging (common commands):
- kubectl (GKE): kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=<service>
- logs: kubectl logs -n platform <pod> --follow --timestamps
- exec: kubectl exec -it -n platform <pod> -- /bin/bash
- Redis: redis-cli -h redis-cluster.platform.svc.cluster.local -p 6379 INFO ALL

Feature flag management:
- Feature flags live in the LaunchDarkly project "redwood-platform". Changes must follow the feature flag change checklist (link in related pages).

3) Dashboards & alerting conventions

Dashboard naming and coverage:
- Dashboards live in Grafana under the "Platform" folder. Naming convention: <service> - Overview; <service> - Errors & Latency; <team> - SLOs.
- All critical services must have an Overview dashboard and an SLO dashboard. Policy: teams have 2 working dashboards per service minimum.

Standard alert severities and examples:
- SevP0 (page): service down / producer-impacting (e.g., control-plane-api 5xx rate > 5% for 3m AND availability < 99.9% over 10m) -> page oncall via PagerDuty and notify #oncall-platform.
- SevP1 (ticket + call): degraded latency/capacity (e.g., inference-router p95 > 500ms for 10m) -> create incident in Incident Manager and escalate to SRE lead if not acknowledged in 10m.
- SevP2 (ticket): warning thresholds (e.g., error rate spike 1-5% over baseline) -> Slack alert to #svc-<service> and ticket to JIRA board PLAT-ops.

Example alert rule (conceptual):
- name: control-plane-api_5xx_surge
  expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane-api",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane-api"}[5m])) > 0.05
  for: 3m
  labels: severity=sevP0, team=platform-core
  annotations: summary="control-plane-api high 5xx rate"

Alerting playbook (on alert):
1. Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty.
2. Triage: check Overview dashboard, recent deploys, and errors log.
3. Run 'kubectl get events -n platform' and check pod restart counts.
4. If crashloop/backoff: capture pod logs and core dump (if available) and attach to incident.
5. If resource pressure: scale replica count or add nodes per scale runbook (see runbooks section).

4) Runbooks (selected, copy-and-paste steps)

A) control-plane-api - HTTP 5xx spike (SevP0)
- Owner: platform-core oncall
- Steps:
  1. Confirm alert and acknowledge.
  2. Check recent deploys (Git commit + tag) in the last 30m: glab pipeline list --status success --since 30m
  3. Inspect errors: kubectl logs -l app=control-plane-api -n platform --since=10m | grep -i error | head -n 100
  4. If a new deploy is implicated, rollback to previous tag: kubectl rollout undo deployment/control-plane-api -n platform
  5. If database saturations apparent, run DB-runbook: confluence/eng-platform/db-runbook-2026.json and scale read-replicas.
  6. Postmortem: start an incident PR in /incidents and follow the postmortem template.

B) inference-router - latency increase (SevP1)
- Owner: serving-routing oncall
- Steps:
  1. Confirm alert, gather p95/p99 graphs and top downstream services.
  2. Check GPU pool capacity: gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels=redwood-gpu-pool"
  3. If KV cache miss rate increased > 20%, inspect kv-cache metrics and consider warming known prefixes.
  4. If throttling due to rate limits, temporarily increase quota for affected tenant via Admin Console and notify product.

C) Redis cluster partial outage
- Owner: infra-caching oncall
- Steps:
  1. Promote a replica if leader failed: redis-cli --cluster call <cluster-host>:6379 CLUSTER FAILOVER
  2. If nodes unreachable, cordon and recreate pods: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  3. Run redis-check --fix and verify dataset consistency.

5) Retrospectives (recent actionable items)

Incident: control-plane-api outage 2026-11-18 (postmortem ref: INCIDENT-2026-11-18-control-plane-outage)
- Summary: Canary deploy of a caching change caused increased 5xx due to missing header assumptions in downstream clients. Recovery took 42m after rollback.
- Action items closed:
  - Add a canary preflight that runs integration smoke tests against canary traffic (owner: platform-core) — done 2026-12-03.
  - Enforce contract tests for header expectations in the API client library (owner: serving-routing) — in_progress.
  - Improve dashboard to show canary vs. baseline error rates (owner: observability) — done.

Retrospective notes & learnings:
- Shorten canary window and add automated rollback on specific error thresholds.
- Increase visibility on downstream header parsing errors (structured logs + alert rule).

6) Roadmap (next 6 quarters — prioritized)

Q2 2027 (near term):
- Complete canary preflight automation (automated smoke + contract tests).
- SLO observability enhancements: add service-level error budget burn dashboards and burn-rate alerts.
- Runbook consolidation: centralize all runbooks in this wiki and tag canonical owners.

Q3 2027:
- Platform autoscaler improvements: predictive scaling for inference-router based on historical traffic patterns.
- Implement tenant-level quotas monitoring and self-service adjustments in the tenant portal.

Q4 2027:
- Private deployment packaging improvements: simplified Helm chart and offline install guide.
- KV-cache region-aware replication for lower tail latency for multi-region customers.

7) Oncall, escalation and ownership

Oncall rota:
- Primary oncall: platform-core (pagerduty schedule: PD-svc-platform-core)
- Secondary: eng-sre (pagerduty schedule: PD-eng-sre)

Escalation path:
1. Primary oncall -> 10 minutes to acknowledge
2. If not acknowledged or unresolved after 20 minutes -> page secondary oncall
3. If unresolved after 60 minutes or customer-impacting -> page platform lead and exec oncall.

Ownership matrix (examples):
- control-plane-api: platform-core (owner: @aisha.rahman@redwood.com), slack: #svc-control-plane-api, pagerduty: PD-control-plane
- inference-router: serving-routing (owner: @liam.oconnor@redwood.com), slack: #svc-inference-router

8) Documentation & templates

- Incident postmortem template: Link: confluence/eng-platform/postmortem-template-2026.json
- Runbook template: copy the runbook sections above — include owner, severity, steps, commands, rollback steps, and post-incident actions.
- Dashboard checklist: include SLO widget, latency histogram, error timeline, recent deploys, and top 10 traces.

9) Maintenance windows and change management

- Planned maintenance should be scheduled in the Maintenance calendar and follow the change-management template. Notify customers via status.redwood.ai with at least 72h notice for infra-impacting changes.

10) Appendix: quick links and resources

- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/Platform
- PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.redwood.internal/schedules/PD-platform-core
- GitLab pipelines: https://gitlab.redwood.internal/infra/platform-cd
- Incident manager & postmortems: https://incidents.redwood.internal

If you are editing this page: please keep a clear changelog at the bottom of the document and add reviewers for any >=sevP1 related changes.
